location: p. 114, Abstract (Conclusions); p. 116, Section 2.3.1; p. 117, Section 2.4
quote: Failure to replicate previous findings of … decreased pain by weak prepulses was most likely due to the sensory modality of the prepulse stimuli.
reason: Neutral locator metadata (single-study replication paper, p. 116, subjective pain ratings) uniquely maps this row to Section 2.3.1 ('Pain intensity ratings', where 'only the pain intensity data are presented'), which conceptually tests the generality of Blumenthal et al.'s (2001) 40–60 ms electrical prepulse pain-reduction effect using weak acoustic prepulses (p. 114: 'Pain induced by electrical stimuli has been found in previous research to be reduced by brief, weak electrical pulses, termed prepulses, presented 40 to 60 ms prior to the painful electrical stimulus. ... The present experiment investigated the generality of this effect by presenting weak acoustic stimuli'). Across the subjective pain rating analyses on p. 116, prepulses slightly increased pain at the 0 ms SOA and had no effect at 80 or 1000 ms ('in contrast to Blumenthal et al. (2001) who found that electrical prepulses decreased pain at SOAs of 40 and 60 ms', p. 117; 'There was no reliable inhibition of pain by the prepulse at any point in time during the session', p. 119), confirming the authors' explicit effect-specific narrative of replication failure on the published archive copy.
